prompt: Stage 3-5. You are level 6 with 46 gold on a win streak of 3, your board is two-starred and beating most of the lobby. Nothing in the shop upgrades you. You are 4 gold off 50. What do you do this round?

options.label: Roll 2–3 times looking for an upgrade; you are winning anyway
Buy nothing, bank to 50+ next round, keep the streak and the interest
Buy the pair of 2-cost bruisers for a future 3-star

explanation:
You are one round from full interest with a board that already wins. Rolling here spends 2 gold per roll at level 6 odds for a shop that is mostly 1- and 2-costs you do not need, and it delays your first 5-interest round by one or two turns. Every round you sit at 50+ is worth 1 gold more than 40+, compounding into the 4-1 level or the 4-2 rolldown. The win streak is doing the work for you: keep it by not touching the board.

Leveling is the second-best option, but 3-5 is early for 7 on a stable board; you want to hit 50 first so that leveling at 4-1 costs you no interest. Buying the bruiser pair is a common Emerald reflex that ties up 4 gold in a unit you will not 3-star without committing to a reroll plan you have not chosen.
principle: 50 gold is a floor you reach as fast as possible, not a target you drift toward.
commonMistake: "Rolling a little" because the board is strong and you feel safe. The safety is exactly why you should not roll: you have nothing to fix.
